question.text: Which of the following accurately describes the permitted fund structures across AIF categories under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: All AIF categories may be open-ended, subject to minimum corpus of INR 20 crore.
Category I AIFs may be open-ended if they invest only in listed equity; Category II and III must be close-ended.
Category III AIFs must be close-ended to qualify for leverage up to 2x NAV; Category I and II may be open-ended.
Category I and Category II AIFs must be close-ended; Category III AIFs may be either open-ended or close-ended at the Manager's discretion at registration.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that Category I and Category II AIFs must be close-ended, reflecting the illiquid nature of their typical investments (start-ups, PE, private credit, infrastructure and similar). Category III AIFs may be structured as open-ended or close-ended, and the choice is fixed at the time of registration based on the intended strategy. The Trap: Option A wrongly says all categories may be open-ended. Option B invents a listed-equity exception for Cat I AIFs and forces Cat II and III into the close-ended bucket. Option C conflates the leverage rule (available to Cat III subject to its own conditions) with the fund-type rule; it is Option C, not the keyed Option D, that confuses leverage with the open-ended/close-ended choice. Note: The clean rule to memorise is: Cat I and Cat II must be close-ended; Cat III may be either open-ended or close-ended, decided at registration; leverage rules for Cat III are a separate question from the structural form.
